summary: The Edinburgh Doctoral College Scholarships are PhD scholarships from the University of Edinburgh for UK and overseas students who start a PhD in the 2027-2028 session. 26 awards are shared across the University's Schools and Colleges. An award pays the University tuition fee and a stipend at the UKRI minimum rate, and includes a training and development package. Nationality, financial status and field of study are not considered.
eligibility_notes:
Open to UK and overseas students starting the first year of an on-campus research degree in 2027-2028. The applicant must have applied for admission to a first year of full-time or part-time, on-campus or distance PhD study at the University. A scholarship application is made after the admission application; the system can take up to five working days to open after the admission application is made. The start date must fall between 1 August 2027 and 31 July 2028 (a start in April 2027, for example, is not eligible).

Candidates must show outstanding academic merit and research potential, and hold or expect a UK first class or 2:1 honours undergraduate degree or an international equivalent. Financial status, nationality and proposed field of study are not considered. Candidates who already hold a PhD or formal equivalent from direct research training are generally not considered.

An award cannot be held with a fully funded scholarship. It can be held with a partially funded one, and the award is then reduced pro rata. English language proof follows the entry requirements of the chosen programme; applicants may apply before they have test results but should upload them as soon as possible. The School of Health in Social Science page gives 23:59 GMT on Monday 9 November 2026 as the date by which the PhD admission application must be made; applicants to other Schools should ask their School about admission deadlines.
age_experience_notes: No age limit is stated. Candidates who already hold a PhD or equivalent from direct research training are generally not considered.
funding_summary: The award covers the University tuition fee and a stipend equal to at least the UKRI minimum rate for the year (GBP 21,805 for 2026/27), plus a training and development package. It lasts between three and four years as agreed by the School (pro rata if part-time), subject to satisfactory progress at annual review. Each School states whether its award is 3.5 or 4 years. Additional project and programme costs are not included. Family leave, medical leave and vacation leave are set in the terms.
programmes_note: PhD research degrees (on-campus or distance study allowed on the admission application) in the participating Schools. The scholarship is offered by Schools of the Colleges of Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences, Science and Engineering, and Medicine and Veterinary Medicine; each School has one award unless noted (Geosciences 3, College of Medicine and Veterinary Medicine 6). Applicants should check that the chosen School takes part; a School that does not take part makes the applicant ineligible.
institutions_note: University of Edinburgh only. Each School runs its own selection and notifies applicants of the outcome. How to apply differs by School: applicants to Arts, Humanities and Social Sciences Schools and to Engineering, Geosciences, Chemistry and Mathematics use the online scholarship form; Informatics and Physics and Astronomy have no separate form because applicants are assessed automatically when they apply for admission; Biological Sciences takes applications directly to the School.

requirements.text: Application for admission to a PhD at the University, made first and through the School's normal route.

The statement cannot be edited after submission; a revised version can be sent before the closing date.

application_steps.title: Apply for PhD admission to a participating School
application_steps.detail: Apply for admission to a first year of full-time or part-time, on-campus or distance PhD study with a start between 1 August 2027 and 31 July 2028. Check admission deadlines with the School; the School of Health in Social Science page gives 9 November 2026 (23:59 GMT). Check that your School takes part in the scheme.

application_steps.title: Submit the scholarship application online before your School's closing date
application_steps.detail: Once the admission application has been processed (up to five working days) log in to MyEd with your University user name and password, start the scholarship application in the student system, choose the scholarship, answer the eligibility questions, write the personal statement and submit. You can apply for only one scholarship at a time. Closing dates are set by School and run from 16 November 2026 to 2 February 2027 (23:59 UK time); late applications are not accepted. Informatics and Physics and Astronomy have no separate form, and Biological Sciences applies directly to the School.

application_steps.title: School assessment and interview
application_steps.detail: The University assesses the scholarship application together with the reference and academic transcript from the admission application, looking for outstanding academic merit and research potential. Shortlisted candidates are invited to an interview, in person or by telephone.

application_steps.title: Outcome from the School
application_steps.detail: The relevant School tells all applicants the outcome. A notification date is not stated. The student system shows the status of each application (for example pending, waiting list, unsuccessful, offer outstanding); an offer comes with an award letter to review before responding.

application_steps.title: Take up the award and keep progressing
application_steps.detail: The award runs for three to four years as agreed by the School and continues subject to satisfactory progress at annual review. Training is required, including Equality, Diversity and Inclusion and Responsible Research. Changing to an ineligible programme, exclusion or withdrawal ends the award; authorised interruption of study can suspend it.

application_steps.title: Submission, extensions and leave
application_steps.detail: A student may submit the thesis early; funding can continue to the end of the quarter in which the thesis is first submitted if work continues, but stops at the original end date if submission is on or after it. Extensions follow UKRI terms. Vacation leave is up to eight weeks a year, with supervisor approval. The University may amend or withdraw any advertised scholarship without notice.
